sections.h2: What should a Keller seller know about the city itself?
sections.html:
Keller is a council-manager city of 18.4 square miles in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, and its city website puts the population at 47,516 as of January 1, 2025. It brands itself as Texas's most family-friendly city, and homes here are marketed on that basis.

Two business districts anchor the city: historic Old Town Keller and the newer Keller Town Center. Big Bear Creek runs through a citywide parks and trail system, and the city operates a recreation and aquatics center called The Keller Pointe. Buyers who tour a house also look at the library, a senior activities center and the police and fire departments, which the city describes as accredited.

sections.h2: Which roads and school district matter when pricing a Keller house?
sections.html:
Keller ISD is the school district, and the city names two primary traffic corridors that shape commute times and noise.

sections.h2: Who appraises and taxes property in Keller?
sections.html:
Tarrant Appraisal District appraises Keller property and administers exemptions, while each taxing unit, such as the city, county or school district, sets its own rate. Tarrant Appraisal District covers seventy-three taxing units across Tarrant County.

The appraisal district says there is no fee for filing an exemption and that it mailed its 2026 appraisal notices to owners. Keep your notice. If you sell after a protest was filed, tell the title company so the outcome is credited correctly.

sections.h2: What do Keller sellers need to know about the Texas tax calendar?
sections.html:
Value is fixed on January 1, bills are mailed around October 1, and a balance still open on February 1 is delinquent.

  • A bill can be paid in two halves, due November 30 and June 30.
  • Late charges are listed on the Comptroller payment page.
  • Homestead applications are generally due by April 30.
  • A homestead appraisal can rise only ten percent a year.

Because the lien dates from January 1, the buyer can inherit that year's bill. The title company divides it at closing. Request a current statement from the Tarrant tax office early in the process.

sections.h2: What homestead and senior breaks can I keep or lose when I sell?
sections.html:
School districts grant a $140,000 homestead exemption, and senior and disabled owners receive $60,000 more plus a cap on their school tax.

A qualifying owner who downsizes inside Texas may carry a proportionate share of that ceiling to the next home. Disabled veterans may qualify for exemptions that range by rating up to a total exemption at 100 percent, and the application window is generous for some of them. Ask the appraisal district to confirm what carries over before you list.

sections.h2: How can a Keller owner sell on a short clock?
sections.html:
Keller owners can choose an agent listing, a sale without one, or a cash buyer. Each costs you time or price in a different way.

  • Listing in a high-value area can bring strong offers, but buyers expect clean inspections and often ask for repairs.
  • Selling alone saves a commission and means you handle showings and contracts.
  • A cash purchase leaves repairs to the buyer and closes when you choose, which helps with a job move, a divorce, renters or an estate.

Run your own numbers, since commission, repairs and months of payments on a listing all reduce what you net.

sections.h2: How does closing and recording work in Tarrant County?
sections.html: The Tarrant County Clerk files a Keller deed in the official records. The clerk will accept it once a notary or similar officer has witnessed the signature, and the manual prices filing page by page plus records fees. The manual's figures date from 2023, so check the current schedule on the Tarrant County Clerk site. The title company normally files at closing.

sections.h2: How do disabled veteran exemptions work for a Keller owner?
sections.html:
Texas scales the disabled veteran exemption to the VA rating, and it applies to one property the veteran owns. A veteran rated 100 percent, including by individual unemployability, can receive a total exemption on the residence homestead, and an unmarried surviving spouse may continue it.

Lower ratings earn smaller dollar exemptions: from $5,000 at a 10 to 29 percent rating up to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent. The usual filing date is April 30, yet Section 11.22 applicants may have up to five years after the delinquency date. Ask Tarrant Appraisal District which forms to file and what it will need from the VA.

sections.h2: What amenities do Keller buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The city lists a library with more than 80,000 items, a new senior activities center beside it, a recreation and aquatics center, Big Bear Creek trails and several sports facilities. Those are the features buyers raise most when they compare Keller to nearby suburbs, so say how far your house sits from them.

The city also reports being named among the best small cities and the safest cities in national rankings, and describes accredited police and fire departments. Use such points carefully in marketing, since buyers will check them. What counts more is the condition of your own lot: roof age, the furnace and the drains.

sections.h2: How are inherited Keller homestead exemptions handled?
sections.html:
An heir whose name is not on a recorded deed has to hand the appraisal district a sworn ownership statement, the death certificate and a utility bill, plus any court citation, before the exemption applies. A buyer who closes after January 1 may claim it at once when the seller had none.

When the owner has died, the deed may come from a death-time transfer deed recorded in advance, an executor's deed, a muniment of title order or an affidavit of heirship, depending on the situation. A county clerk cannot add heirs to an old deed on its own.

sections.h2: Does Keller have anything unusual about its government or growth?
sections.html:
The city is run by a council with seven places, including the mayor, and a city manager handles day-to-day operations. At 18.4 square miles it is a compact suburb, which means most neighborhoods are older than the newest Tarrant County growth areas and buyers often compare Keller resale houses to new construction in neighboring cities.

The city website calls Keller Texas's Most Family-Friendly City and says the community pairs big-city conveniences with small-town roots. For a seller, the takeaway is that school zoning, park access and trail connections will be the first questions on a showing, so have the answers ready.

sections.h2: What if my Keller house has tenants, a mortgage default or an open estate?
sections.html:
Each of these three situations adds a step before closing. A default letter starts a short clock under the Texas foreclosure process, and the auction is held on a first Tuesday at the courthouse. An open estate needs a court order or an affidavit before anyone can sign a deed. Renters need proper written notice, and a justice court handles the eviction suit.

Some cash buyers take a house with renters or an unsettled estate, though a Texas attorney should look over the plan first.

faqs.a: The City of Keller lists 47,516 residents as of January 1, 2025, within 18.4 square miles.
Keller is in Tarrant County, so Tarrant Appraisal District handles appraisals and exemptions, and deeds are recorded with the Tarrant County Clerk.

faqs.q: Does Tarrant charge to file an exemption?
faqs.a: No. Tarrant Appraisal District states there is no fee for filing an exemption. Apply by the April 30 deadline for most exemptions.

faqs.q: What date makes a Texas tax bill late?
faqs.a: Most bills become delinquent on February 1 after being mailed around October 1. The Comptroller's payment page lists the penalty and interest that begin that day.

faqs.q: Is a no-repairs sale possible in Keller?
faqs.a: Yes, through a cash buyer; a loan-backed buyer may still ask for repairs. Disclose known problems either way, and check permits on past work.
